Also
AWL-soh
adv.
Old English eallswā: all + so. Webster 1828: likewise; in like manner. His illustration is Matthew 6:21: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. The KJV uses it for God’s extra work in creation, for the heart that follows its treasure, for the disciples where Christ is, for heirs glorified with Him, and for the brother who must be loved if God is loved.

Biblical Definition

Also in Scripture is not a throwaway conjunction. It binds a second thing to the first by the same rule. Genesis does not treat the stars as an afterthought of mood; he made the stars also (Gen 1:16). The same God who ruled day and night with two great lights made the host as well. Jesus will not let the heart pretend independence: where your treasure is, there will your heart be also (Matt 6:21). The place He prepares is not a separate destiny: that where I am, there ye may be also (John 14:3). Union with Christ has a matching clause in suffering and glory: that we may be also glorified together (Rom 8:17). Love of God is not allowed to stop at the vertical: he who loveth God love his brother also (1 John 4:21). The dictionary therefore keeps also from becoming additive religion — one more spiritual accessory. It is the same Lord, the same treasure, the same Christ, the same commandment, arriving at the next lawful place.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines ALSO as an adverb from all and so: likewise; in like manner. He quotes Matthew 6:21 as the illustration: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

expand to see more

AL'SO, adverb [all and so.] Likewise; in like manner.

Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Matthew 6:21.

Webster refuses a second heart. The adverb does not add a mood. It locates the same heart where the treasure already is.

Key Scripture

Genesis 1:16 — "And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also."

Matthew 6:21 — "For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also."

John 14:3 — "And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also."

Romans 8:17 — "And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together."

1 John 4:21 — "And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also."

Modern Corruption

Also is corrupted when it becomes extra-credit religion, when the heart is treated as free of its treasure, and when love of God is allowed to float without the brother.

expand to see more

The first corruption is additive religion. Genesis 1:16 is not God tacking on décor. The stars are the same day’s work. Therapeutic religion loves also as a second program — Jesus plus a technique, grace plus a brand. The recovery is one Creator and one finished day.

The second corruption is to split treasure from heart. Matthew 6:21 will not permit a compartment. Inspirational talk pretends you can store money, applause, or platform in one place and keep a pure heart in another. Jesus says the heart will be also wherever the treasure already is. The adverb is a verdict, not a motto.

The third corruption is a God-love that will not travel. First John 4:21 makes the brother the test. Sentiment can praise God and despise the man beside it. The commandment does not offer a second, softer love. He who loves God loves his brother also — the same love arriving at the next lawful object.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English eallswā (all + so). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek kai (G2532) at Matthew 6:21, John 14:3, Romans 8:17, and 1 John 4:21. Genesis 1:16 is untagged in this cache; no Hebrew number is invented for he made the stars also. The companion entry likewise already treats the parallel adverb; this page is the English also.

expand to see more

Greek kai (G2532) — and, also, even (Matt 6:21; John 14:3; Rom 8:17; 1 John 4:21).

Romans 8:17 also tags glorified together as syndoxazō (G4888) beside also (G2532).

Genesis 1:16 untagged in this cache — no Hebrew number is minted for also.

Usage

"He made the stars also (Gen 1:16) — the same God, the same day, not a second religion."

"The heart will be also where the treasure is (Matt 6:21); the adverb is a verdict."

"He who loves God loves his brother also (1 John 4:21); vertical talk that will not travel is not love."
